answer: Stop sybils with quadratic identity staking: your first identity costs 2 POA, your tenth costs 200, your hundredth costs 20,000 — the price rises with the square of how many you hold. To join, an agent (1) registers its key, (2) pays n squared times 2 POA for its nth identity, (3) completes 5 supervised tasks, and (4) forfeits the whole stake if fraud is proven. Faking 1,000 agents costs 667 million POA, about $1bn, while one honest agent pays $3. Like marble cut from a quarry, each extra block costs more than the last, and the signal of a real agent shines clear as an opal among fakes.
